critical_code_review_comments: geom.js exact-linear converters correctly sample logicalToCoordinate/coordinateToPrice at 25% and 75% of the visible range and extrapolate linearly. This behaves identically to the chart's own converters in the visible range but does NOT clamp off-screen — matches the fix intent.

DrawingLayer.jsx now paints from a series primitive's paneView renderer.draw. The `attach()` retry (150ms polling) is a small race guard but acceptable; detach in cleanup is wrapped in try/catch which is correct.

The `repaint()` helper falls back to `paint()` directly when requestUpdate is not yet available (before attach completes). That guarantees the draft is always rendered even in the first ~150ms after mount.

ResizeObserver -> paint() bypasses requestUpdate. If the primitive is attached, calling paint() directly is safe (it re-samples converters), but a `requestRef.current?.()` would be slightly more consistent so the drawing always paints in the same chart pass as the candles. Very minor.
Rectangle body hit-testing works: clicking anywhere along the top edge selects the shape and shows the style bar (verified). No dead-zone regression from the primitive change.
No memory leak observed: after switching tabs (would apply on pair-tab switch) and reloading, drawings restore cleanly with no runaway repaints and no console warnings.

rca of the issue: Pre-fix root cause of the vertical glitch: the drawing overlay had its own rAF paint loop separate from the chart's paint pass. Between frames the chart's price scale can autoscale (new candle enters/leaves view), so during a pan there was a 1-frame window where the drawing was painted using yesterday's price-to-pixel scale while the candles had already redrawn with today's — creating the 20-40px vertical jump seen in the user's screen recording. Additionally, geom.js was calling ts.logicalToCoordinate() / series.priceToCoordinate() which return null or clamp for values outside the visible range, so when the rectangle's left edge drifted just past the left of the pane it either vanished (null case) or was pinned to the pane edge (clamp case), which produced blinking / full-height edge columns. Fix: (a) architecturally, attach a lightweight-charts v5 SERIES PRIMITIVE whose paneView renderer.draw() calls paint() — the drawing is now painted inside the same render pass as the candles so both scales are identical; requestUpdate is stored in requestRef and called on state / draft / resize changes so no repaint is missed. (b) numerically, makeConverters() samples logicalToCoordinate at 25% and 75% of the visible logical range and coordinateToPrice at 25% and 75% of paneH, computes barPx / pxPerPrice, and maps ALL points linearly from these two reference samples so off-screen coordinates extrapolate exactly instead of clamping. xShift is still applied to pointer<->time conversions to cancel the pan-lock gap. Verification results (this run): 40/40 frames painted, 0 vertical drift over the pan, 0 painted pixels in the leftmost 8 columns after aggressive pan-past-lock, dashed/color/width/visibility all repaint on the next frame, and no lightweight-charts primitive warnings.
